similar_questions.stem: Which of the following statements **is not true** about exhalation?

questions.stem: Adaptation is the process by which:

options.A: new varieties of plants are selected for use in agriculture.
options.B: organisms become better suited to their environment.
options.C: individuals of one species interact with individuals of another species.
options.D: a reflex reaction occurs in response to an unusual stimulus.

explanation_steps: Adaptation is the process that makes organisms better suited to their environment. Answer: B.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following statements define the term population?

options.A: All living things in the same area that interact with one another.
options.B: Groups of organisms of the same species inhabiting the same area.
options.C: All living organisms interacting with non-living environment.
options.D: The biological role played by a species in its environment.
options.E: A place where individuals of a species live.

explanation_steps: A population is a group of individuals of the SAME species living in the same area at the same time.
Textbook (G12 p.87): 'The place where a population or an individual of a given species lives is called a habitat. The biological role played by a species in its environment is called a niche.'
A = community; C = ecosystem; D = niche; E = habitat. Answer: B.

similar_questions.stem: In ecological studies, a community refers to:

options.A: a group of individuals within a species living in a particular place at the same time.
options.B: the complex of interactions between living and non-living parts of the environment.
options.C: a group of families within a species living in a particular place at the same time.
options.D: an extended family which depends upon one another for food and shelter.
options.E: populations of organisms that live together in a specific area and depend upon one another.

explanation_steps: A community is the populations of different species living together in one area.
A is a population; B is closer to an ecosystem. Answer: E.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is not true of cell theory?

options.A: The cell is the structural unit of life.
options.B: The cell is the unit of function of living things.
options.D: The molecules of life are the products of cellular activity.
options.E: Cells are surrounded by a cell wall.

explanation_steps: Cell theory does not claim that every cell has a wall. Animal cells have a membrane but no wall.
A–D are standard statements of cell theory. Answer: E.
tips: This question asks for the one that is NOT true. Check every option, cross out the true ones, and choose the one left.
Think about what the part or process does (its function). The right option matches that function.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following statements **is not** true about cells?

options.A: The cell is the basic unit of all living organisms.
options.B: Eukaryotic cells have evolved from prokaryotic cells.
options.C: Cellular biomolecules are the product of cell activities.
options.D: All cells have similar structure and function.

explanation_steps: While all cells share some basic features (like a plasma membrane and ribosomes), they are not all similar in structure and function. Cells are highly specialized (differentiated) to perform specific roles, such as nerve cells for signals and red blood cells for oxygen transport.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following statements is not part of the Cell Theory?

options.A: All life is made of cells.
options.B: Cells are the smallest units of life.
options.D: All cells have mitochondria for energy production.

explanation_steps: The cell theory has three statements: all living things are made of cells; the cell is the smallest (basic) unit of life; all cells come from pre-existing cells.
Mitochondria are not in the theory – and prokaryotic cells (bacteria) have no mitochondria at all. Answer: D.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: Plant cells are usually smaller than animal cells.
options.B: Animal cells tend to be more distinct in shape than plant cells.
options.C: Cytoplasm takes up most of the space in an animal cell.
options.D: Glycogen is stored in plant and animal cells.
options.E: Starch is stored in animal cells.

explanation_steps: Animal cells lack a large central vacuole, so cytoplasm occupies most of the cell.
Plant cells are usually larger and more regular; glycogen is animal storage; starch is plant storage. Answer: C.
tips: Watch reversed roles (who attacked whom) and swapped names/countries.

similar_questions.stem: Which statement best describes the relationship between adaptation and natural selection?

options.A: Adaptations occur randomly and do not influence survival.

similar_questions.stem: Which one of the following **is not** true about transpiration in plants?

options.A: pulls water from root to leaves.
options.C: increases turgor pressure in the cells.
options.D: is the evaporation of water from the leaves.

explanation_steps: Transpiration is the loss of water vapor from leaves. This loss actually **decreases** turgor pressure in cells. It creates a 'pull' (tension) that brings more water up from the roots.
